title: Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management
outcomes: Read forex quotations, spreads, cross rates and forward points.
Identify transaction, translation and economic exposure.
Hedge with forwards and money market hedges and handle forward contract fates.
Use futures, options, swaps and structured products within an exposure strategy.

meta.exam_tip: Convert annual rates to the period before applying IRP or money market hedges.

concepts.title: Forex market, quotations and cross rates
body: The forex market is a global over-the-counter market linking banks, corporates, central banks and dealers via systems like SWIFT for secure messaging. Banks hold nostro (our account with you), vostro (your account with us) and loro (their account with you) accounts, and manage both exchange (currency) positions and cash (fund) positions.

Quotes: direct (home currency per unit of foreign, e.g. ₹84/USD) or indirect (foreign per unit of home); American and European terms. Bid is the dealer's buying rate, ask its selling rate; spread = ask − bid. Cross rates are derived through a common currency: buy at the bank's bid, sell at its ask.
Forward rates are quoted as points added (premium) or subtracted (discount) from spot; broken-period rates are interpolated. Merchant rates for customers (TT, bill buying/selling) build in margins.
concepts.analogy: Read every quote from the bank's side: it buys low and sells high.
concepts.work: If USD/INR is 84.00/84.10, a customer buying USD pays ₹84.10.

concepts.title: Exchange rate theories: IRP, PPP and IFE
body: Interest rate parity (IRP): forward ÷ spot = (1 + home interest) ÷ (1 + foreign interest) for the period. The higher-interest currency trades at a forward discount. Deviations allow covered interest arbitrage.

Purchasing power parity (PPP): absolute — the same goods cost the same everywhere; relative — expected change in spot rate reflects the inflation differential: S₁ = S₀ × (1 + home inflation) ÷ (1 + foreign inflation).

International Fisher effect (IFE): expected change in spot rate reflects nominal interest differentials. IRP holds well (arbitrage); PPP and IFE hold more loosely and over longer periods. Forecasting uses these parities plus technical and fundamental analysis.
concepts.analogy: Interest and inflation gaps explain where currencies should move.
concepts.work: With Indian rates 7% and US 4%, the dollar trades at a forward premium of about 3% a year.

concepts.title: Types of foreign exchange exposure
body: Transaction exposure: risk that rate changes alter the home value of contracted foreign currency receipts or payments (imports, exports, loans) before settlement.
Translation (accounting) exposure: effect of rate changes on consolidated statements when foreign subsidiaries' accounts are translated; it affects reported figures, not necessarily cash.

Economic (operating) exposure: effect of rate changes on future cash flows and competitive position — e.g. a rising rupee hurting exporters' long-term margins even without current contracts. It is harder to hedge and needs operational responses (sourcing, pricing, location).
concepts.analogy: Transaction hits cash now, translation hits reports, economic hits the future business.
concepts.work: An exporter facing cheaper foreign rivals has economic exposure.

concepts.title: Hedging tools and the fate of forward contracts
body: Internal techniques: invoicing in home currency, leading and lagging, netting, matching receipts and payments, and asset-liability management. External techniques: forwards, money market hedges, futures, options and swaps.

Money market hedge: for a payable, deposit the PV of the foreign amount now (borrowing home currency to buy it); for a receivable, borrow the PV in foreign currency and convert now. Compare with forward cost.

Fate of forward contracts: delivery (on due date, early or late), cancellation (on due date, early or late) or extension. Under FEDAI rules, cancellation is at the opposite TT rate (TT selling for a purchase contract cancelled, etc.), with the exchange difference and any swap cost or interest settled with the customer; overdue contracts not cancelled are automatically cancelled after a set period, losses recovered and gains not passed on. Non-deliverable forwards settle only the difference; rollovers extend deliverable contracts.
concepts.analogy: Hedge with internal tools first, then markets — and know how forward contracts end.
concepts.work: An importer cancelling a forward early settles the difference at the opposite rate.

concepts.title: Derivative products and exposure strategies
body: Currency futures and options trade on exchanges; options give one-way protection (call for importers, put for exporters) for a premium. Currency swaps exchange principal and interest in different currencies; interest rate swaps convert fixed to floating flows.

Structured bank products include forward importer/exporter contracts with knock-out levels, FX call and put options, and floating-to-fixed IRS on foreign loans; their pay-offs must be understood at different spot outcomes.

Exposure management strategies range from low risk–low reward (hedge everything), low risk–reasonable reward (selective hedging), high risk–low reward (selectively not hedging) to high risk–high reward (actively trading exposures). Policy should fit the board's risk appetite.
concepts.analogy: Pick tools that match the exposure and the board's appetite.
concepts.work: An exporter buys a USD put to protect against a falling dollar while keeping upside.

illustrations.title: Forward rate and cross rates
illustrations.q: (a) Spot USD/INR is ₹84.00. Six-month interest rates are 7% p.a. in India and 4% p.a. in the US. Compute the 6-month forward rate by interest rate parity and the annualised forward premium on USD. (b) USD/INR is 84.00/84.10 and EUR/USD is 1.0800/1.0810. Compute the EUR/INR two-way quote.

viva.model: The forward rate divided by the spot rate equals one plus the home interest rate divided by one plus the foreign interest rate for the same period.
Transaction exposure affects contracted cash flows already agreed; economic exposure affects future cash flows and competitiveness.
Invoicing in home currency, leading and lagging, and netting or matching.

viva.q: What are the possible fates of a forward contract?
viva.model: Delivery, cancellation or extension — each on the due date, early or late.
An exchange of principal and interest payments in one currency for those in another currency.
